# ADR 0060 — The UI platform: Tailwind's vocabulary, generated by Helix; markup next

- **Status:** Accepted — Phase 1, the style engine, is implemented in `src/style.rs`.
- **Date:** 2026-11-08
- **Deciders:** Areeb + Claude
- **Related:** [ADR 0055](0055-apps.md) (the app runtime), [ADR 0056](0056-design-engine.md)
  (design tokens), [ADR 0057](0057-gestures.md), [ADR 0058](0058-motion-v3.md),
  [ADR 0059](0059-rich-interactions.md).

## Context

The goal is that anyone can build beautiful, rich apps with Helix, more easily than with React,
shadcn/ui and Tailwind.

**What that stack gets right:**
- **Tailwind** is a vocabulary of class names that everyone, and every code-writing AI,
  already knows.
- **shadcn** gives you components you own and can change, built on accessible behaviour
  primitives.
- **React** composes components in markup (JSX), and reloads them while they run.

**What it gets wrong:**
- A toolchain (Node, a bundler, PostCSS) before the first pixel.
- Design tokens that know nothing about contrast or nested corners.
- Animation and accessibility added from separate libraries.
- State spread across hooks.
- No way to replay a UI, or test one without a browser.

Helix has the other half:
- one binary with no build step;
- an app that is a pure model, replayable on three engines, with hot reload that keeps state;
- a design engine that computes colour with proven contrast and corners that nest
  (ADR 0056);
- springs, gestures and shared elements built in;
- a page script that never runs app code.

What it lacked was a way to style a view without writing CSS, and a way to write views that
reads like markup.

## Decision

The platform has six layers:

1. **Utility classes:** Tailwind's names, generated by Helix (this ADR, Phase 1).
2. **Markup:** a JSX-like syntax that the parser turns into the same view data (Phase 2).
3. **Behaviour primitives:** dialog, popover, menu, combobox, tabs and slider, accessible
   and unstyled. Most already exist in the page script.
4. **Components** built from layers 1–3, in the new look, that a project can copy and own
   (`helix ui add`), with variants as data.
5. **Tools:**
   - a dev overlay that inspects any element's classes and tokens;
   - a gallery generated from the components' docs;
   - screenshot tests from replays;
   - accessibility lints in `helix check`.
6. **Templates** for whole apps.

### Phase 1: the style engine

An app writes Tailwind's class names: `p-4 rounded-xl bg-accent hover:bg-accent/90
md:grid-cols-3`.

- **When a view renders,** the runtime collects the class names it uses (`view_classes`, in
  Rust). `utility_css` writes the CSS for those that are utilities, once each.
- **What the page receives:**
  - its first load carries the stylesheet for the classes its view uses;
  - a frame whose view adds new classes carries the stylesheet for every class seen so far
    (`util`);
  - a frame that adds none carries nothing.
- **Classes are only ever added,** so a node that is still leaving never loses its rule.
- **There is no build step, and no Node.** Unknown names produce nothing, as in Tailwind.

The vocabulary is Tailwind v4's, with Tailwind's values: its spacing scale (`--spacing:
0.25rem`), type scale, radii, shadows, blurs, breakpoints, containers, and its palette exactly,
taken from the published `tailwindcss@4.3.5` package. It covers:

- **Layout:** display, position, inset and z-index; flex and grid (including spans and
  starts); gap and space.
- **Box:** padding and margin (with negatives), sizing (including fractions, `screen` and
  containers).
- **Type:** size (with `/leading`), weight, tracking, leading, alignment, `truncate`,
  `line-clamp`, case and decoration.
- **Paint:** colour with `/opacity`, gradients (`bg-linear-to-r from-… via-… to-…`), borders,
  per-side radii, shadows, rings with offsets, opacity, filters and backdrop filters.
- **Motion and interaction:** transitions, durations and easings, scale, rotate and
  translate, `animate-spin`/`ping`/`pulse`/`bounce`, `sr-only`, cursor, `select`, `touch`,
  scroll snap, `aspect`, `object`, `divide`.

Variants:
- states: `hover:` (only where hover exists), `focus:`, `focus-visible:`, `active:`,
  `disabled:`, `first:` and the other child positions, `open:`, `placeholder:`, `*:`;
- `group-*` and `peer-*`;
- `dark:`;
- breakpoints `sm:` … `2xl:` and `max-*:`, and container queries `@sm:` …;
- `data-[state=open]:` and `data-active:`, `aria-selected:` and the other ARIA states;
- `motion-safe:`/`motion-reduce:`, `contrast-more:` and `print:`.

Also `!` for important and a leading `-` for negative values.

**Helix's design tokens join the vocabulary under their own names,** so a utility follows the
app's design, light and dark, as the components do:
- colours: `bg-accent`, `text-muted`, `border-line`, `bg-surface-2`, `text-danger`,
  `bg-card` (material-aware) and the other roles;
- the concentric radii and paddings: `rounded-card`, `rounded-control`, `p-card`;
- elevations: `shadow-1` to `shadow-3`;
- type styles: `text-title-2` and the others;
- springs: `ease-spring`.

A plain `border` is coloured `--line`, not `currentColor`, and a plain ring is coloured
`--focus`.

### Where utilities sit in the cascade

The components' stylesheet is in the `hx-components` cascade layer and the utilities are in
`hx-utilities`, declared after it. So a utility on a component always applies, whatever the
component selector's specificity. An app's own `style:` is unlayered and beats both. The
library's own layout classes moved out of the utilities' way:

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `grid` | `hx-grid` |
| `gap-N` | `hx-gap-N` |
| the `outline` button variant's class | `outlined` |
| `ring` | `progress-ring` |

`html` keeps the browser's own font size, so a `rem` (the unit of the scale) follows the
person's setting; the body carries the type. A zero-specificity reset (`:where(...)`) removes
list markers and indents, and buttons' platform chrome, as Tailwind's preflight does, without
outranking any component.

### Safety

A class name can come from data. These guarantees hold:

- Only a name that parses as a known utility produces CSS.
- An arbitrary value (`w-[320px]`, `grid-cols-[1fr_2fr]`) must pass a whitelist:
  - letters, digits, `#%.,_()+-*/` and space only;
  - balanced parentheses;
  - no `url(`, `image-set(`, `expression(`, `attr(` or other functions that fetch or run.
- Every selector is fully escaped.
- Non-ASCII and control characters produce nothing.

So a class can never close its rule, open a new one, or fetch anything. The corpus
(`tests/corpus/ui_utilities.helix`) and a live CLI test try thirteen such classes; none
produces CSS.

## Consequences

- **The gallery's "Utility classes" card is written only in utilities:**
  - a pricing grid that becomes three columns from `md:`;
  - cards that lift on a spring;
  - a highlighted plan with a ring and a badge;
  - token colours that switch with dark mode.
- **The browser test checks real computed values:**
  - `p-6` is 24 px;
  - `rounded-card` equals the design's radius;
  - three columns at desktop width;
  - the hover lift;
  - no collision with component classes;
  - axe passes.
- **Cost.** CSS is generated only when a view first uses a class: about 6 KB for the gallery's
  utilities. A frame that introduces no utility sends nothing extra.
- **Not yet:**
  - arbitrary properties (`[mask-type:alpha]`);
  - `@apply`;
  - theme extension from an app;
  - `before:`/`after:` content.

  Each needs care about what an app can inject.
- **Next:** Phase 2, markup. Then the new-look components on these layers, with
  `helix ui add`.
